sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json -> {{rd|melee|ranged}} template convention, cross-checked against items whose melee/ranged split is unambiguous
sources_quoted.quote: Tiamat :: {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} ; Ravenous Hydra :: {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} ; Titanic Hydra :: {{rd|4%|2%}} ; Hullbreaker :: {{rd|10%|{{ap|10*0.7}}...}}
sources_quoted.inference: First argument of {{rd|...}} is the MELEE value, second is the RANGED value (Tiamat/Ravenous cleave is 40% AD melee / 20% ranged; Titanic Hydra crescent is 4% max health melee / 2% ranged). Hence Expose Weakness = +8% damage taken (melee wielder), +5% (ranged wielder).

sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

Black Cleaver average stacks (`ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction`): the established model uses a fixed `0.8*max_stacks` constant ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp `min(k, C)` over `h` hits is `C - C(C-1)/(2h)` for `h >= C`; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes.
the mitigation operator `x -> x*100/(100+R)` is *linear in raw damage* for a fixed resistance

independent_computation.step_0_what_the_leaf_is: `pair_damage` on a combat event of a *coupled* scenario is damage attributed to the paired participant, not to the Bloodsong/Cleaver wielder. Therefore only a TARGET-SIDE amplifier (a debuff on the victim) can move it. Scanning every amplifier in data/items.json, exactly one is target-side and phrased 'from all sources': Bloodsong's Expose Weakness (S1). Every other amplifier in the cache is wielder-side and cannot touch a partner's damage: Lord Dominik's Regards ('Deal ... increased damage'), Riftmaker (2%/s, 8% cap, self), Haunting Guise (6%, self), Liandry's Torment (6%, self), Spear of Shojin (self ability/pet/proc damage), Immortal Path (4%, self), Perplexity (self), Diamond-Tipped Spear (self). Press the Attack (data/runes.json, damage_amp_ratio 0.08) is also wielder-side ('grant you 8% increased damage against champions').

step_1_observed_ratio.rounding_bracket: Displayed values are 1-dp. old in [94.05, 94.15), new in [101.65, 101.75) => the true multiplicative factor lies in [1.079660, 1.081871].

step_2_candidate_factors.hypothesis: Expose Weakness applied at the MELEE value: x1.08
step_2_candidate_factors.result: NON-EMPTY -> FEASIBLE. A true old value of e.g. 94.14 rounds to 94.1 and 94.14*1.08 = 101.67 rounds to 101.7.

step_2_candidate_factors.hypothesis: Expose Weakness applied at the RANGED value: x1.05
Correction of ranged->melee value (x1.05 replaced by x1.08, net x1.02857)
Black Cleaver stack model change (constant 0.8*5 = 4.0 stacks = 24% armor reduction -> Cesaro mean -> up to 5 stacks = 30%), per S3/S5
step_2_candidate_factors.result: RULED OUT — no League target carries ~2000 armor, and any percent/flat penetration in the build shrinks the ratio further, so the Black Cleaver stack model cannot produce an 8.08% jump. (Also: a BC change would alter the wielder's own mitigation on the victim, which does move pair_damage too, but not by this magnitude.)

independent_computation.step_3_conclusion: The only factor consistent with both the rounding bracket and the cached wiki text is exactly x1.08 = Bloodsong's Expose Weakness at its melee value (S1 + S2). The old leaf carried no Expose Weakness amplification on the partner's damage; the wiki text says the debuff makes the target 'take 8% increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES', which by its plain wording includes the paired participant's damage. Uptime is not a rescue for the old value: the debuff lasts 4 s and re-applies on a 1.5 s Spellblade cooldown, so in a sustained fight (event index 48) it is effectively permanent.
independent_computation.reconstructed_identity: pair_damage_new = pair_damage_old * (1 + 0.08) ; with raw damage d and post-penetration resistance R, the engine's mitigation is linear in raw (S6), so the target-side amplifier composes as a clean scalar: post = d * 100/(100+R) * 1.08 (S4).
independent_computation.numeric_check: 94.14 (a value that displays as 94.1) * 1.08 = 101.67 -> displays as 101.7. Consistent to the last displayed digit.

verdict_reasoning: new_value_correct. The 8.08% jump is the Bloodsong 'Expose Weakness' target-side amplifier at its cached melee value of 8%, which the old leaf omitted from the paired participant's damage even though the cached wiki text says 'take 8% increased damage from all sources'. The old value is unambiguously missing a sourced effect; the new value reproduces it exactly (x1.08) within 1-dp rounding.
caveats: The melee/ranged branch is set by the Bloodsong WIELDER (S2). The new value is exact for a melee wielder (+8%). If the roster's Bloodsong holder were ranged, the sourced factor would be +5% and the correct leaf would be ~98.8, making both values wrong. I could not read the scenario definition (it is not under data/; it lives in scripts/, which this runbook forbids), so the wielder's range class is inferred, not read: the scenario pairs Black Cleaver — a melee bruiser item requiring repeated physical-damage application to stack Carve (S3) — with Bloodsong, and 1.08 is the value the engine actually used; 1.05 is arithmetically impossible for this leaf pair. On the evidence available, melee is the supported reading.

This receipt does not attempt to reconstruct the absolute magnitude 94.1/101.7 from first principles — champion, level, build, and target stats are defined outside data/. The claim verified is the multiplicative identity between old and new, which is sufficient to adjudicate the leaf against the cached source text.
